memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You are to skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces. The sons of Aaron the priest are to put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.'" - Lev 1:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The burnt offering was unique among the sacrifices. In most offerings, part was eaten by the priests or the worshipper. Not this one. The whole animal went up in smoke. The Hebrew name for it, olah, means "that which ascends." Nothing was kept back.

So the animal is skinned and cut into pieces, and the fire is prepared. It is slow, deliberate, physical work. There is no rushing through this.

The burnt offering was fundamentally about total consecration — the worshipper saying to God, I am entirely Yours, without reserve. That is a costly thing to say honestly. Most of us are willing to give God a portion. We hand over Sunday and keep Monday. We surrender our reputation but hold our finances. We give Him our future plans while keeping a private area of the heart marked "not for inspection."

Jesus offered Himself wholly. He held nothing back, being obedient to death — even death on a cross (Phil 2:8). And He calls His followers to a whole-life response, not a partial one (Lk 9:23). Paul knew this well: I no longer live, but Christ lives in me (Gal 2:20).

What piece of your life have you not yet placed on the altar?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which area of my life have I quietly kept off the altar?
2. Am I giving God portions of myself, or my whole self?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I confess how carefully I ration myself out to You. Take the parts I have withheld, and let my whole life ascend to You. Amen.
